'''Dewayne "D. J." White Jr.''' (born August 31, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player, who was selected in the first round of the [[2008 NBA draft]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=9}}, he played the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position. He played for parts of six seasons in the NBA, before continuing his career playing overseas. He is currently the general manager of the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] in the [[NBA G League]].

==Early life and college==
A [[Hillcrest High School (Tuscaloosa, Alabama)|Hillcrest High School]] standout, White led all freshmen in the Big Ten Conference in scoring during his freshman season with the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]].<ref name="scoring">{{cite web |url=http://iuhoosiers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/white_dj00.html |title=D.J. White |publisher=IUHoosiers.com |date=November 1, 2007 |access-date=February 10, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080214115325/http://iuhoosiers.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/white_dj00.html |archive-date=February 14, 2008 }}</ref> He was named by [[Rivals.com]] as a Freshman All-American, and was named a 5-star recruit by [[Scout.com]]. He was also selected as the Big Ten Freshman of the Year. In 2008, he was named Big Ten Player of the Year and to the First Team All-Big Ten.<ref name="POY">{{cite web |url=http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080310/SPORTS/80310071 |title=IU's White: conference player of year |publisher=Indianapolis Star |date=March 10, 2008 |access-date=March 10, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319203838/http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20080310%2FSPORTS%2F80310071 |archive-date=March 19, 2012 }}</ref> He was also named Second Team All-American in 2008.<ref name="AllAmer">{{cite web | url = http://blogs.heraldtimesonline.com/iusp/?p=1788 | title = Sporting News names D.J. White a second-team All-American | publisher = IUHoosiers.com | date = March 12, 2008 | access-date = March 18, 2008 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110711163213/http://blogs.heraldtimesonline.com/iusp/?p=1788 | archive-date = July 11, 2011 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
White was drafted with the 29th pick of the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]] and traded the same day to the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], who were relocating to [[Oklahoma City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2008/06/pistons_trade_firstround_pick.html|title=Pistons trade first-round pick|publisher=www.mlive.com|date=June 26, 2008|author=A. Sherrod Blakely|access-date=April 28, 2009}}</ref> White's rookie season was delayed when he had to undergo surgery on his jaw to remove a benign growth, causing him to miss the first five months of the season.  He finally made his professional debut for the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]] on March 18, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/a-thunder-star-waiting-in-wings/article/3355483|title=A Thunder star waiting in wings?|publisher=www.newsok.com|work=The Oklahoman|date=March 23, 2009|author=Darnell Mayberry|access-date=March 23, 2009}}</ref> In six games he played with Tulsa, he averaged 18.3 points and 7.2 rebounds per game. After that short stint, he was recalled by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] and made his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut on April 5, 2009, against the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290405025|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120717113821/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290405025|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 17, 2012|title=Indiana Pacers vs. Oklahoma City Thunder - Recap - April 5, 2009|publisher=www.espn.com|work=ESPN|date=April 5, 2009|agency=Associated Press|access-date=April 28, 2009}}</ref> During his rookie season, White played in seven games for the Thunder and averaged 8.9 points and 4.6 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whitedj01.html|title=D.J. White statistics|publisher=www.basketball-reference.com|access-date=April 28, 2009}}</ref>

In the 2009–10 season, White appeared in eight games with Oklahoma City, averaging 4.8 points and 1.9 rebounds, before requiring surgery in January to repair a fractured thumb. After recovering, White was once again assigned to the Tulsa 66ers on March 4, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/65137/20100304/thunder_assign_white_to_d_league/ |title=Thunder Assign White To D-League |access-date=March 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100308220330/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/65137/20100304/thunder_assign_white_to_d_league/ |archive-date=March 8, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was recalled just five days later on March 9 after averaging 23 points and 11 rebounds in four starts for Tulsa.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/65232/20100309/oklahoma_city_recalls_dj_white/ |title=Oklahoma City Recalls DJ White |access-date=March 9, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100311193623/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/65232/20100309/oklahoma_city_recalls_dj_white/ |archive-date=March 11, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On March 21, White received a standing ovation upon entering the contest during an away game against the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the state where he played in college.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/recap_pacers_100321.html Recapping the Thunder's 121-101 loss to the Indiana Pacers]</ref> White scored six points and grabbed two rebounds in 10 minutes of playing time during the game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20100321/OKCIND/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |title=March 21, 2010 Oklahoma City-Indiana Box Score |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 4, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100411143136/http://www.nba.com/games/20100321/OKCIND/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore |archive-date=April 11, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  White returned to the 66ers on April 7, 2010.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html 2009-10 transactions] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101144313/http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html |date=November 1, 2011 }}</ref> For a total of 10 games he played for Tulsa that season, he averaged career-highs of 20.2 points and 11.1 rebounds in 39.2 minutes per game on the court. He even appeared in one NBA D-League playoff game for them, scoring 21 points, and having 5 rebounds and 4 assists.

For the beginning of the 2010–11 season, White was retained on the Thunder's 15-man roster, with the Thunder exercising its fourth-year contract option on White on October 25, 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/options_release101025.html |title=Thunder Exercises Options on Six Players |date=October 25, 2010 |access-date=October 27, 2010 |work=www.nba.com/thunder |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. }}</ref> On February 24, 2011, White and [[Morris Peterson]] were traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for [[Nazr Mohammed]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2011.trade.deadline.tracker/index.html |title=2011 trade deadline tracker |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=February 24, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110225162253/http://www.nba.com/news/transactions/2011.trade.deadline.tracker/index.html |archive-date=February 25, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In September 2012, White signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of China.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.shanghaisharks.cn/cms/ArticleView.aspx?id=500 |title=上海东方篮球俱乐部-新闻 |access-date=September 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929005234/http://www.shanghaisharks.cn/cms/ArticleView.aspx?id=500 |archive-date=September 29, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 28, 2013, White signed a 10-day contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-dj-white |title= Celtics Sign D.J. White| work=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2013| access-date=March 20, 2013}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract with the Celtics on March 10, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-white-second-10-day-contract |title=Celtics Sign White to Second 10-Day Contract| work=NBA.com|date=March 10, 2013| access-date=March 20, 2013}}</ref> On March 20, 2013, White was signed to a multi-year contract by the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-white-multi-year-contract|title=Celtics Sign White to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 20, 2013|access-date=March 20, 2013}}</ref>

On July 12, 2013, he was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] as part of the blockbuster deal that brought [[Kevin Garnett]] and [[Paul Pierce]] to Brooklyn.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-acquire-nba-champions-kevin-garnett-paul-pierce-and-jason-terry|title=Nets Acquire NBA Champions Kevin Garnett, Paul Pierce and Jason Terry|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=October 15, 2013}}</ref> He was subsequently waived by the Nets on July 18.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/nets-waive-dj-white|title=Nets Waive D.J. White|work=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2013|access-date=October 15, 2013}}</ref>

In September 2013, White joined the [[Chicago Bulls]] for their training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14338 |title=Patrick Christopher, Mike James, Dahntay Jones, Kalin Lucas, Dexter Pittman and D.J. White in Bulls training camp |access-date=September 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029191020/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14338 |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he was waived on October 26.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14655 |title=Chicago Bulls waive Dexter Pittman, D.J. White |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195950/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14655 |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In November 2013, he signed with the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] for the 2013–14 CBA season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sichuan announced DJ White|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/68077/sichuan-announced-dj-white.html|access-date=December 5, 2013|work=Sportando.net|date=November 23, 2013}}</ref>

On March 21, 2014, he signed a 10-day contract with [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-forward-dj-white-10-day-contract Bobcats Sign Forward DJ White to 10-Day Contract] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331191535/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-forward-dj-white-10-day-contract |date=March 31, 2014 }}</ref> On March 31, 2014, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Bobcats.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bobcats Sign Forward DJ White to 2nd 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-forward-dj-white-2nd-10-day-contract|access-date=March 31, 2014|newspaper=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407045053/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-forward-dj-white-2nd-10-day-contract|archive-date=April 7, 2014}}</ref> On April 10, 2014, he signed with the Bobcats for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-forward-dj-white-remainder-season Bobcats Sign Forward DJ White for Remainder of Season] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413123615/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-forward-dj-white-remainder-season |date=April 13, 2014 }}</ref>

On October 4, 2014, he signed a one-month deal with [[Saski Baskonia|Laboral Kutxa Vitoria]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Laboral Kutxa refuerza su juego interior con la llegada del ex NBA Dewayne White|url=http://www.baskonia.com/laboral-kutxa-refuerza-su-juego-interior-con-la-llegada-del-ex-nba-dewayne-white/|access-date=October 4, 2014|work=baskonia.com|language=es}}</ref> On November 7, 2014, he parted ways with Laboral Kutxa after his contract expired.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/140263/dj-white-leaves-baskonia.html DJ White leaves Baskonia]</ref> On November 25, 2014, he signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] of China for the rest of the [[2014–15 CBA season]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/142459/fujian-signs-dj-white-parts-ways-with-al-harrington.html |title=Fujian signs DJ White, parts ways with Al Harrington |access-date=November 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150215225853/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/142459/fujian-signs-dj-white-parts-ways-with-al-harrington.html |archive-date=February 15, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 7, 2015, White joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the 2015 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cavs Announce 2015 Samsung NBA Summer League Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/summer-league-roster-2015|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2015}}</ref> On August 26, 2015, he signed with [[Auxilium CUS Torino]] of Italy for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=ECCO IL LUNGO CHE COMPLETA IL ROSTER, E' D.J. WHITE Jr. |url=http://www.auxiliumcustorino.com/Article.Detail/?UserKey=ECCO-IL-LUNGO-CHE-COMPLETA-IL-ROSTER-E-D-J-WHITE-Jr- |access-date=February 19, 2016 |work=auxiliumcustorino.com |date=August 26, 2015 |language=it |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119180815/http://www.auxiliumcustorino.com/Article.Detail/?UserKey=ECCO-IL-LUNGO-CHE-COMPLETA-IL-ROSTER-E-D-J-WHITE-Jr- |archive-date=January 19, 2016 }}</ref> On July 22, 2016, he re-signed with Torino for one more season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/207272/dj-white-returns-to-torino.html DJ White returns to Torino]</ref>

On July 8, 2017, White signed with the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]] club [[Gaziantep Basketbol]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/240455/gaziantep-basketbol-signs-dj-white.html Gaziantep Basketbol signs D.J. White]</ref> On December 6, 2017, he left Gaziantep and signed with the [[Turkish Basketball First League]] club Bahcesehir Basketbol.<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/turkey/tbl/256549/dj-white-leaves-gaziantep-to-sign-in-turkish-second-division-with-bahcesehir-basketbol.html DJ White leaves Gaziantep to sign in Turkish second division with Bahcesehir Basketbol]</ref>

In 2019, White joined [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]]. He averaged 9.2 points, 2.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game. He re-signed with the team on August 22, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=White re-signs at Tofas |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/641898/White-re-signs-at-Tofas |website=Eurobasket |access-date=September 4, 2020 |date=August 22, 2020}}</ref>

In January 2022, White signed with the [[Daegu KOGAS Pegasus]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] to replace [[Cliff Alexander]] for two weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title='알렉산더 대체' 가스공사, 새 외인 DJ 화이트 영입 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065613821635110 |website=점프볼 |access-date=January 6, 2025 |date=January 12, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=한국가스공사, 알렉산더 2주 진단…니콜슨 복귀 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065572906673853 |website=점프볼 |access-date=January 6, 2025 |date=January 19, 2022}}</ref> On February 1, Cliff Alexander was replaced by White for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=한국가스공사, 알렉산더→화이트 시즌 대체로 교체 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065588975540262 |website=점프볼 |access-date=January 6, 2025 |date=February 1, 2022}}</ref>

On July 11, 2022, White signed with the [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN)<ref>{{cite web |title=Quebradillas sign D.J. White, ex KoGas |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/756251/Quebradillas-sign-D.J.-White,-ex-KoGas |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=October 16, 2024 |date=July 11, 2022}}</ref>

On August 15, 2022, he has announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/d-j-white-announces-retirement/|title=D.J. White: Announces retirement|last=|first=|date=August 15, 2022|website=|publisher=CBSsports|language=En|access-date=August 20, 2022}}</ref>
